coordinator_questions.a_equity_common_for_clo_equity: Not decided here, for the owner. The published asset_category enum has LOAN, DEBT, EQUITY_COMMON, EQUITY_PREFERRED, FUND, OTHER, CASH; there is no CLO-equity value (CLO_EQUITY appears only in an exception list in pipeline/source_reconciliation.py and is never assigned). Cohort convention in data/output/private_markets_holdings.parquet: CLO subordinated/income notes are LOAN with index_classification and asset_class STRUCTURED_CREDIT, 899 rows across 13 funds (incl. BCRED before this run); the only EQUITY_COMMON rows matched (Great Elm, 9) are not CLO notes. So BCRED is now the only fund publishing CLO equity tranches as EQUITY_COMMON. index_classification and asset_class are STRUCTURED_CREDIT in both cases, so headline donuts keyed on index classification do not change; export_frontend.py does not read asset_category. Trade-off: EQUITY_COMMON matches the filer's 'Equity Instruments' heading and the residual risk of the tranche, but it puts par-denominated notes into the equity population, which is what creates the 5 new C04 / field_coverage_drop findings. LOAN (cohort convention) avoids that but calls equity risk a loan; DEBT or OTHER are the other existing values. A dedicated value would be a schema change.
coordinator_questions.b_reclassified_rows_vs_printed_section: Checked all rows, not a sample. Of 15,499 published rows, 1,698 lie inside a printed Structured Finance Obligations span: all 1,698 are STRUCTURED_CREDIT; 265 of them lie inside the '- Equity Instruments' sub-span and all 265 are EQUITY_COMMON (223 changed LOAN to EQUITY_COMMON, the rest were already equity); no row outside the spans is STRUCTURED_CREDIT. 5 rows not located (Minerva, and four zero-value CFCo/Pigments rows). Agrees with the agent's 1,698.
coordinator_questions.c_41_unit_counts: All 41 (2024-09-30 to 2025-03-31) print the figure unscaled in the 'Par Amount/Units' column of a schedule in thousands (e.g. '20,000,000 18,000 18,417'), and the iXBRL tags it us-gaap:InvestmentOwnedBalanceShares, unitRef shares, scale 0 (Galaxy 34 c-1101). So the filer calls it a unit count. Caveat: the same figure was already published as principal_amount (20,000,000) in bcpc and still is, so these rows carry it in both fields. That is consistent with $1-denominated notes, but it is one figure counted twice.

finding_reviews.rationale: The mechanism is supported. At 2025-06-30 the 33 equity tranches without a count carry only InvestmentOwnedBalancePrincipalAmount (scale 3), printed in thousands. The fund-quarter key '0001803498|2025-06-30|unit count on equity' is the right coverage. The quantitative claim is wrong, and it is repeated in the hypothesis and in PD-0001803498-C04-2 ('12.5 points under the prior quarter'). In the shadow ledger, 12.5 is field_coverage_drop's metric violation_pct over n_units 8: one of eight fields failed. It is not the size of the drop. On the rule's basis (published rows, fair value > 0, asset_category EQUITY%), unit-count coverage falls from 100.0 pct of 87 rows at 2025-03-31 to 67.0 pct of 100 rows at 2025-06-30, about 33 points. The owner would be accepting a disposition with a wrong number; correct it in the hypothesis and the proposal. Owner context: the finding exists only because of the EQUITY_COMMON class choice (question a).

observation_reviews.rationale: I am withdrawing my own round-one premise that this check has no false-alarm risk; it was wrong. In bcpe every BCRED row with a maturity date except the 6 corrected ones is maturity_status 'unresolved' with precision 'unknown': 22,361 rows. The 6 corrected rows (now 'dated'/'day') are the only 'dated' rows of the fund. In the cohort build, 278,033 rows across 127 funds are 'unresolved' with a valid date. So the proposed check ('unresolved' with a valid YYYY-MM-DD date) would flag 22,361 BCRED rows and about 278K cohort rows, and the fix makes 6 rows inconsistent with the rest of the fund. The real issue is fund-wide (or shared): maturity precision is not established for BCRED's tagged maturities. The observation should be re-diagnosed on that basis (why 'unknown' precision; is 'unresolved' the intended status for tagged dates), and the 6-row maturity_precision correction reconsidered until then.
